newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Baht steady ahead of reference rate news.
newsitem.headline: Baht steady ahead of reference rate news.

text.p: The offshore baht was basically steady in early Asian business after Wednesday's plunge but it did have a softer feel to it ahead of Thursday morning's 0130 GMT announcement of the new dollar/baht reference rate.

The onshore rate had yet to be quoted but stood at 27.250/250 late on Wednesday. In the offshore market quotes from Australia had it at 29.000/30.000, also little changed from late Wednesday, but it had earlier edged down to 29.400/30.400.
Thailand's adoption of a managed float system will include the setting of a daily reference rate and the 0130 GMT announcement will be the first.
"We'll have to see what the rate is but as it's being set in terms of the onshore rate we can expect it to be around 27.50 or higher," said one trader.

"But it still remains to be seen whether the 'appropriate rate' they are talking about could be a little lower. There is still a chance they will try and claw some of yesterday's drop back," he added.
